compatibility.title: Which Mitsubishi Models Use the 4B11 2.0 MIVEC?
compatibility.intro: The 4B11 was developed as part of the Global Engine Manufacturing Alliance (GEMA) alongside the Hyundai G4KD and Chrysler ECN. In Mitsubishi form, it features MIVEC variable valve timing on the intake camshaft (and on both camshafts in some applications). The naturally aspirated 4B11 was the most popular petrol engine in the Lancer, Outlander and ASX ranges during its production run, offering 145-150 hp.

costGuide.title: Mitsubishi 4B11 2.0 MIVEC Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 4B11 typically takes 8-10 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Mitsubishi specialist) - the transverse four‑cylinder layout is relatively straightforward, though the timing chain and MIVEC system add moderate complexity.【PATTERN DATA】
paragraphs: The biggest price movers for a 4B11 replacement are timing chain and tensioner condition (stretch is common beyond 90,000 miles), oil consumption history (valve guide wear), and MIVEC phaser health. Engines with documented timing chain replacement and regular oil changes command a premium. See our full /prices/reconditioned-engine-cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Mitsubishi 4B11 2.0 MIVEC Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Consumption - valve guide and piston ring wear
items.whatHappens: The 4B11 is considered a very reliable engine, but at higher mileage it is prone to oil consumption. This is typically due to wear on valve guides and seals, or the occurrence of piston ring sticking. At mileages beyond 125,000 miles (200,000 km), increased oil consumption is commonly observed. Symptoms include the need for frequent top‑ups between oil changes, blue smoke from the exhaust on startup, and in severe cases, fouled spark plugs.
items.repairVsReplace: Valve guide and seal replacement requires cylinder head removal (£600-£1,200). If piston rings are worn, a full engine strip is required (£1,500-£2,500). If oil consumption is severe (1 litre per 1,000 miles) or has led to scored cylinder bores, a full replacement is often the most cost‑effective solution. Read our full /failures/oil-consumption guide

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - the most critical wear item
items.whatHappens: The 4B11 uses a timing chain rather than a belt. The chain is designed to last the life of the engine under normal servicing, but poor oil quality, high mileage or neglected oil changes can cause the chain to stretch. When the chain stretches, the ECU may log fault codes for cam timing correlation. Symptoms include a rattle on cold start, rough idle, and in severe cases, the triangle warning light appearing. If the chain stretches beyond safe limits, it can jump a tooth or more, causing valves to contact pistons - catastrophic engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement costs £500-£1,000 including chain, guides, tensioner and sprockets. If the chain has jumped and bent valves, a full replacement engine is required - this is an interference engine. Read our full /failures/timing-chain-failure guide

items.title: MIVEC System Issues - phaser and solenoid faults
items.whatHappens: The 4B11's MIVEC system uses oil pressure to actuate cam phasers. Over time, the MIVEC solenoids can become clogged with oil sludge, or the phaser sprockets can wear. Symptoms include a reduction in power and economy, rough running, and in some cases, a Check Engine light with MIVEC‑related codes. On turbocharged 4B11T engines, the exhaust MIVEC cam gear housing is known to fail under increased valve spring pressure - though this is less common on the naturally aspirated 4B11.
items.repairVsReplace: MIVEC solenoid cleaning or replacement costs £150-£300. Phaser sprocket replacement is more involved (£400-£800). Regular oil changes with the correct 5W‑30 specification are the best prevention.

items.title: Drive Belt Tensioner Failure - a known recall item
items.whatHappens: The 4B11's accessory drive belt automatic tensioner flange can crack, allowing the drive belt to detach. This was the subject of a recall on some 2011-2012 Lancer models. If the belt detaches, the battery will discharge and the engine will stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
items.repairVsReplace: The tensioner should be replaced with the improved design as part of routine maintenance (£150-£300). If the belt has already detached, the belt, tensioner and any damaged pulleys should be replaced.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 4B11 has been in production since 2006, with continuous refinements. The engine is considered very reliable overall, with an estimated lifespan of approximately 350,000 km (217,000 miles). The timing chain was revised in 2011 with a redesigned version featuring fewer links to reduce friction. Later production engines (2012+) benefit from improved chain durability and updated ECU calibration. The 4B11 is significantly more reliable than the older 4G69 and 4G63 engines it replaced, offering better fuel economy and lower emissions.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 4B11 2.0 MIVEC
variants.intro: The 4B11 is a Specific engine code covering Mitsubishi's 2.0‑litre naturally aspirated MIVEC engine. Unlike Family pages that cover multiple fundamentally different engines, this page covers the 4B11 as a single engine with multiple output tunes and applications. It is important to distinguish it from the turbocharged 4B11T found in the Lancer Evolution X, which has different internals and a semi‑closed deck. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block - typically on the front, just below the cylinder head, or on the driver's side of the block. It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (e.g. 4B11xxxxxx). Use a Mitsubishi VIN decoder to confirm the exact variant from the build sheet. Key 4B11 variants: | Variant | Power | Torque | Key Difference | Applications | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4B11 (148 hp) | 148 hp (108 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 197 Nm @ 4,200 rpm | MIVEC on intake only | Lancer ES / GTS (US market) | | 4B11 (150 hp) | 150 hp (110 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 200 Nm @ 4,200 rpm | MIVEC on both intake and exhaust | UK/EU Lancer, Outlander, ASX | | 4B11 (145 hp) | 145 hp (107 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 195 Nm @ 4,200 rpm | Lower‑output tune, different ECU | Outlander CW, ASX early models | Why fitting the wrong variant matters: While all 4B11 variants share the same basic architecture (1,998 cc, 86.0 mm bore × 86.0 mm stroke, 10.0:1 compression), they have different ECU calibrations and, in some cases, different MIVEC phaser configurations (single vs dual MIVEC). Fitting a single‑MIVEC engine into a dual‑MIVEC vehicle will result in reduced performance and potential drivability issues. Commonly confused codes: | Engine Code | What it is | Why it's confused | |---|---|---| | 4B11T | Turbocharged 2.0L (Evo X) | Same displacement but semi‑closed deck, forged internals, different ECU - not interchangeable | | 4B10 | 1.8L MIVEC | Smaller displacement, different stroke - lower power | | 4B12 | 2.4L MIVEC (167 hp) | Larger displacement (2,360 cc), different bore/stroke - not a direct swap | | 4J11 | 2.0L successor engine | Later engine with different architecture - not interchangeable |

relatives.description: the 2.4‑litre SOHC engine that preceded the 4B11 in many Outlander and Lancer applications. A cast‑iron block, belt‑driven engine producing 160 hp in its highest tune. The 4G69 was reliable but heavier and less fuel‑efficient than the 4B11. The 4B11's all‑aluminium construction and DOHC MIVEC design represented a significant step forward in power delivery and efficiency.

the 2.0‑litre successor engine introduced in later ASX and Outlander models from approximately 2015. Features a different valvetrain design and updated emissions technology. Not a direct swap into 4B11‑equipped vehicles without significant modification.

the legendary turbocharged variant of the 4B11, used in the Lancer Evolution X (2007-2016). Features a semi‑closed deck block, forged internals, different oil jets, and a different ECU. Produces 280-320 hp. While the block is similar, the 4B11T is not a direct swap into a naturally aspirated 4B11 car without extensive modification (turbocharger, ECU, fuel system, cooling). Many Lancer owners consider the 4B11T as an upgrade path, but it requires significant work.

the 1.8‑litre (1,798 cc) variant of the 4B family, used in the Lancer (1.8 MIVEC) and ASX (1.8 MIVEC) in certain markets. Produces 138-140 hp. Shares the same block architecture but has a different bore/stroke and ECU calibration. Not a direct swap for the 4B11.

the 2.4‑litre (2,360 cc) variant of the 4B family, used in the Outlander (2.4 MIVEC) and certain Lancer models. Produces 167 hp and higher torque. Shares the same architecture but has a longer stroke and different ECU. The 4B12 is often considered a worthwhile upgrade for Lancer owners, offering better torque without the complexity of turbocharging - but requires ECU calibration changes.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 4B11 2.0 MIVEC - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 4B11 can be a cost‑effective option for lower‑value host vehicles (sub‑£3,000 Lancer, ASX) - but only if the engine comes with documented proof of timing chain replacement and regular oil change history. Given the engine's known weaknesses (timing chain stretch, oil consumption), a used unit without history is a gamble - chain stretch is not "if" but "when" on higher‑mileage examples. Used prices from £1,000-£1,500 reflect this risk. Link once:

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned 4B11 is the recommended choice for most Lancer, Outlander and ASX owners. A full recon should address the engine's known weak points: new timing chain, tensioner and guides (revised 2011‑spec kit), new valve guide seals (to address oil consumption), new piston rings, MIVEC solenoid and phaser inspection, and full gasket set. Given the £1,700-£2,500 supply cost and the host vehicle value (£2,000-£8,000 for a decent Lancer, £3,000-£10,000 for an Outlander/ASX), this represents a significant but justifiable investment. A 12-24 month warranty is essential. Link once:

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full 4B11 rebuild is justified for low‑mileage, well‑maintained examples or where the owner plans long‑term ownership. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing chain, oil pump, and a full valvetrain refresh. Rebuild costs (£2,500-£3,500+) are significant - only consider this for high‑value or sentimental vehicles. Link once:

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All supply options can be fitted through our network of vetted Mitsubishi specialists nationwide, with a minimum 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units and full nationwide delivery coverage. Fitting costs typically range from £700-£900. Link once:
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 4B11 sits in host vehicles ranging from £1,500-£5,000 (older Lancer CY, Outlander CW) to £4,000-£12,000 (ASX, later Outlander GF, Eclipse Cross)【THIRD‑PARTY - AutoTrader UK market data 2025】. A £1,700-£2,500 reconditioned unit represents 20-70%+ of the vehicle's value on many examples - on a £2,500 Lancer, a £2,000 replacement is 80% of the vehicle's value, making it a borderline decision. The honest marketplace‑neutrality position is: if your 4B11 has suffered catastrophic failure (timing chain jump causing valve damage, severe oil starvation) and your vehicle is worth under £3,000, evaluate scrap or part‑exchange value before committing to a replacement. For well‑maintained, low‑mileage examples with good bodywork and service history, the replacement can be a worthwhile investment. The 4B11's longevity - up to 350,000 km (217,000 miles) with proper maintenance - means many examples are still on the road and worth saving.【THIRD-PARTY】

items.question: Is the 4B11 2.0 MIVEC reliable, and what mileage can I expect?
items.answer: The 4B11 is considered a very reliable engine with an estimated lifespan of approximately 350,000 km (217,000 miles) with proper maintenance. It is significantly more reliable than the older 4G69 and 4G63 engines it replaced. However, like all engines, it requires diligent maintenance - regular oil changes using 5W‑30 specification oil are critical, particularly given the timing chain's dependence on oil quality. Budget for timing chain inspection around 90,000-120,000 miles. Drive belt tensioner should be replaced with the improved design as a preventative measure. The 4B11's all‑aluminium construction and chain‑drive design make it a robust, long‑lasting engine. The 4B11T (turbocharged Evo X) variant shares the basic block but has different internals and is not covered on this page.
